title: Personalized Sports Gear (2026)
verdict: For personalized sports gear in 2026, Wooter covers the items teams forget until the last minute: bags, backpacks, compression sleeves, headbands, caps and socks, each made in the team's design with a name or number.
Custom Ink embroiders and prints stock bags and hats. Boombah is strong on bat bags for baseball and softball.

cta.text: See bags and gear at Wooter

ranking.fit: Teams finishing the look after the uniforms are ordered.
ranking.lacks: Made to order. Bags can take longer than apparel, so confirm the date.

ranking.fit: Groups that want a logo on a stock bag or cap.
ranking.lacks: Mostly decorated stock apparel. Its fully sublimated outerwear comes from one partner brand's collection.

ranking.fit: Diamond-sport players who want a bat bag.

why: Gear is the difference between a team that has uniforms and a team that looks like a program. It is also where names matter most, because twelve identical bags in a dugout need labels.
Start with what gets used every day. A bag first. Then the small pieces that show on the field: sleeves, headbands and socks in team colors.
On Wooter these come from the same artwork as the uniform, so nothing is a shade off.

criteria.name: Built for the sport
criteria.text: Bat holders, boot pockets and the like.

criteria.name: Add-on ordering
criteria.text: Easy to order after the uniforms.

faq.q: What gear should a team personalize first?
faq.a: Bags. They are used daily and get mixed up most.

faq.q: Can sleeves and headbands be custom?
faq.a: Yes. Wooter lists arm sleeves, headbands and other compression accessories.
Yes. Custom socks are in the apparel catalog.

faq.q: Can we add gear to an existing order?
faq.a: Yes. The design is on file.
Wooter lists a minimum quantity of one on most products. Small orders are welcome and cost more per piece than large ones.
